argument_summary: The admissible record supports a narrower position than clean compliance: certification is supportable on a caveated basis because the current release passed aggregate readiness by 2.2 percentage points and had no severity-one rehearsal incidents, but the grant-compliance slice regressed below the warning threshold and the record does not show approved mitigation or attached disclosure language. On that record, the defensible theory is not that prior approval or informal monitoring closes the gap; it is that certification can be treated as supportable only if the current-release packet is read as requiring explicit disclosure of the material limitation for the named launch use case.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost claim is needed to support this position. The request is based on risk-weighted treatment of the admissible governance record, not on launch-pressure considerations.
claims_about_policy: Policy does not allow prior family approval or an informal monitoring note to substitute for current-release evidence. The admissible policy text instead supports a narrower treatment: aggregate readiness supports the release on the merits, while the material subgroup weakness must be disclosed unless covered by approved mitigation or formal risk acceptance. Because the current record shows the weakness and the disclosure obligation, the clean-compliance claim is too broad; the policy-consistent position is caveated compliance tied to current-release disclosure, not rejection of certification outright based solely on aggregate-readiness evidence.
concessions: The current record does not prove that the required current-release disclosure language is already present in the model card or launch documentation.
The current record does not show approved mitigation or formal risk acceptance for the grant-compliance regression.
Prior approval of an earlier family release is contextual only because the current release has a different retrieval configuration and evaluation batch.
The informal post-launch monitoring comment cannot be treated as equivalent to approved mitigation, owner acceptance, or documented disclosure.
